Chapter 12: The Pleasures of God and the Hope of Glory.
Have you ever noticed that quiet longing deep down—the feeling that there should be more to life, a hope for a world finally made right? It’s the kind of thing you hear in the stories we tell, the songs people sing, and those late-night prayers whispered when no one else is listening.
That longing? It’s not a mistake. It’s actually a signpost, pointing us toward something real—the hope of glory.
For a lot of folks, the world just feels broken. There’s disappointment, loss, and sometimes it seems like real joy is out of reach. The pleasures of God can feel far away—almost impossible to imagine. But the story’s not finished yet. The hope of glory is this powerful promise: one day, everything will be made new. The same joy God’s always experienced will flood the world, and all those deep longings? They’ll finally be satisfied.
Picture someone who keeps hoping, keeps loving, keeps believing—even when life gives them every reason to quit. That kind of hope isn’t just wishful thinking. It’s grounded in who God is, in the rock-solid certainty of His promises, and in the reality of His joy.
It’s become clear—the pleasures of God aren’t just for this life. They’re the foundation for a hope that lasts, a joy that can’t be stolen away. There’s a promise that one day, every tear will be wiped away, every sorrow turned into joy, and every broken thing made whole again.
Sure, it’s easy to fall into despair or cynicism, to feel like giving up is the only option. But the real truth is so much stronger. The hope of glory is the assurance that the story ends in joy, that God’s pleasures will fill the earth, and every longing will be met.
And here’s why it matters right now: hope changes how we live. It becomes a source of strength, a reason to keep moving forward, a light that cuts through the darkness. The pleasures of God turn into our anchor, our promise, and the song that carries us through every season.
